This table defines the three parameters you use when opening or switching the “input” database in the DB command. It tells you what each parameter is, how it behaves, what units (if any) it uses, and which default value applies if you omit it. In practice, you can close the current database and open a new one simply by supplying these items in your command string. See also SIZ2 for related database-sizing options.

1. NUMB  
   • Description: “Reference number of the database.”  
     – When you specify NUMB, you tell the system which numbered database to open as your new input.  
     – If you set NUMB = 0, the command will reuse the database that was active at the start of the input session.  
   • Unit: none  
   • Default: 1  
   • Notes: Only supply a nonzero reference if you previously defined that database by giving it a TITL (path/name) in an earlier command. Otherwise the system assumes you want database #1.

2. INIT  
   • Description: “Initialization of input.”  
     – INIT determines whether current view-related settings and group or box definitions carry over to the newly opened database.  
     – INIT = NO preserves existing VIEW, GRP, BOX, and other settings so you can directly compare models across databases.  
     – INIT = YES resets these settings, which is useful when you’re loading a fresh FEM section or want a “clean slate.”  
   • Unit: LIT (literal keyword)  
   • Default: NO  

3. TITL  
   • Description: “Path and name of the database.”  
     – Specify the actual filename or full pathname of your external database if it hasn’t been defined yet.  
     – Once you give a TITL, you can later refer to that database simply by its NUMB.  
   • Unit: LIT (literal string)  
   • Default: * (none)  

How it fits together:  
When you issue a DB command with these parameters, the system first closes whatever database is currently open. Then, if you supply a TITL, it reads that file in and assigns it the NUMB you gave. If you only supply a NUMB (and no TITL), the system expects that database slot to have been defined earlier. Finally, INIT governs whether any prior display, grouping, or box definitions carry over to your newly opened database. By default (INIT=NO), everything stays as is; but in specialized FEM workflows or when you want guaranteed clean initial settings, you’d set INIT=YES. This flexible mechanism lets you load multiple databases under a unified modeling session and quickly switch among them for direct comparison.  
See also the SIZ2 command for additional database sizing and management options.

See also: SIZ2
 DB
 The current database is closed and the new input database is opened with the input DB. Only the reference number of the database has to be input in the case of previous definition of this database with TITL.
 In this case WING is searched in the first database for a FEM database of cross section ’no’.
 The current settings, .e.g. VIEW, GRP or BOX, are not changed (INIT NO). Thereby is it possible to compare databases with similar systems directly. But in some cases, e.g. FEM section, an initialization of input is useful (INIT YES).

This table defines the key parameters you need to set up page size, scaling, margins, frames and legend areas when generating drawings or plots in GRAPHIC.  It is organized into four columns—Item, Description, Unit and Default—and covers everything from raw paper dimensions to the style of the outer border.  Below is a walkthrough of each entry, its purpose, the units you supply (if any), and the default behaviour when you omit it:

1.  TYPE  
    •  Purpose: Selects the paper format or free-form size.  
    •  Behavior:  
       – A positive value (or literal without “–”) picks the named format in landscape orientation.  
       – A negative value (prefixed “–”) picks the same format in portrait orientation.  
       – Acceptable literals include standard DIN 0…6, ANSI A…D, Hewlett-Packard series HPA…HPD, MP, LP, MPW, or the special REPORT BROWSER (“URS”) and the current Windows printer (“WIN”).  
    •  Unit: Literal (LIT)  
    •  Default: WIN (the last interactive Windows printer)

2.  SC  
    •  Purpose: Establishes the drawing scale.  
    •  Options:  
       •  0 – fill the chosen page format as large as possible; scale is calculated automatically.  
       •  – (dash) – choose the best engineering scale (1:1, 1:2, 1:5, …) to fill the page.  
       •  * (asterisk) – lock to the explicitly supplied scale value (if feasible).  
    •  Unit: none  
    •  Default: “–” (best engineering scale)

3.  W  
    •  Purpose: Explicit width of the paper in centimeters.  Overrides TYPE if specified.  
    •  Unit: cm  
    •  Default: none (must be provided if you require a custom width)

4.  H  
    •  Purpose: Explicit height of the paper in centimeters.  Overrides TYPE if specified.  
    •  Unit: cm  
    •  Default: none

5.  MARG  
    •  Purpose: Controls whether and how the program draws borders and margins around your plot area.  
    •  Options:  
       •  OFF – no border is drawn at all.  
       •  NO – only an inner border plus scale is drawn; W and H define the plotting extents (suitable for single-sheet plotters and laser printers).  
       •  YES – includes a free border around the drawing, with 2 cm margin if W/H were set, otherwise 0.5 cm.  
       •  FULL – draws an additional outer border at the paper limits (intended for drum plotters).  
    •  Unit: Literal (LIT)  
    •  Default: FULL

6.  FORM  
    •  Purpose: Chooses the shape and annotation style of the frame or title block.  
    •  Options:  
       •  STAN – Standard drawing frame (pictures only).  
       •  ZTVK – ZTVK-88 style frame (pictures only).  
       •  URS  – REPORT BROWSER frame (for tables and pictures; includes no external margin).  
    •  Unit: Literal (LIT)  
    •  Default: URS

7.  HLEG  
    •  Purpose: Height of the reserved legend area located immediately under the plot.  Use this to ensure space for HEAD lines or picture legends.  
    •  Unit: cm  
    •  Default: 1.0

8.  WLEG  
    •  Purpose: Width of the reserved legend area to the right of the plot.  If you need a sidebar legend or additional HEAD lines arranged vertically, increase this.  
    •  Unit: cm  
    •  Default: 0.0

Notes on using these parameters together:  
- If you omit both W and H, TYPE (and possibly SC) alone determines paper size and orientation.  
- Setting either W or H to zero lets GRAPHIC pick the complementary dimension for you, based on the chosen scale.  
- MARG and FORM work in concert to define outer and inner margins, title bands and where your HEAD lines (created with SCHH, ZTVK, etc.) will appear.  
- HLEG and WLEG then carve out exactly how much room is reserved inside those margins for your plot legends or titles.

By carefully combining these eight fields, you control every aspect of page layout—from raw format selection and scaling logic to the style and size of borders, frames and legend areas—ensuring consistent, reproducible drawings across any output device.

This table is the definition of the SIZ2 record (with its companion SCHH, COLO, LEGO and AND records) in the SOFiSTiK/GRAPHIC RAG‐vector environment. It specifies how paper, scale, margins and sub‐plots are set up before plotting.  Below is a field‐by‐field description suitable for ingestion into a vector‐store with retrieval‐augmented‐generation (RAG) indexing:

1. TYPE  (STRING)  
   • Paper format code.  
   • Allowed values:  
     – DIN sizes “0” through “6” (default landscape).  
     – Preceding “–” selects portrait.  
     – URS/–URS: REPORT BROWSER format (no external margin).  
     – WIN/–WIN: Windows/graphic‐printer default.  
     – Numeric “9”/–“9”: free format using explicit W,H.  
     – ANSI: A/–A, B/–B, C/–C, D/–D.  
     – HP: HPA, HPB, HPC, HPD, HP4, HP3, HP2, HP1 (with optional minus).  
     – MP/–MP: matrix printer 8×12 in.  
     – LP/–LP: laser printer A4.  
     – MPW: wider matrix 14×12 in.

2. W, H  (REAL, default mm or inch)  
   • Explicit paper width (W) and height (H).  
   • If both nonzero, TYPE may be “9” or overridden.  
   • If one dimension is zero, scale + one dimension determines the other.  
   • If both zero, TYPE (or internal selection) picks standard format.

3. SC or SCAL  (REAL)  
   • Drawing scale (e.g. 1:1, 1:2, 1:5, …).  
   • If omitted or set to zero, program chooses the largest feasible scale given W,H and engineering‐scale grid.

4. DRUL, DRUR, DRDL, DRUU  (REAL)  
   • External “print” margins:  
     – DRUL = distance from left edge.  
     – DRUR = distance from right.  
     – DRDL = bottom margin.  
     – DRUU = top margin.  
   • If omitted, GRAPHIC uses printer defaults.  
   • Only active for formats other than URS.

5. FORM  (STRING or literal)  
   • Internal partitioning/layout mode.  
   • Common value: STAN – positions HEAD lines between inner/external margins.  
   • ZTVK – produces a two‐band title‐block on A4 portrait.

6. Subdivision code  (literal “HxW”)  
   • Splits paper into multiple plots in a grid of H×W boxes.  
   • H,W are digits 1–9 or letters A–G (10–16).  
   • Plots are filled left‐to‐right, top‐to‐bottom; or via AND record to jump.

7. WLEG, HLEG, SLEG  (REAL)  
   • Legend margins and band sizes:  
     – WLEG: right‐side legend margin width.  
     – HLEG: text‐band height.  Negative HLEG places legend on left.  
     – SLEG: overall legend height (per‐plot).

8. SCHH  (record grouping)  
   • Text‐height settings for:  
     – H1: HEAD‐line height.  
     – H10: picture‐legend line height.  
     – If more legend lines are needed, user may reduce H1/H10.

9. COLO, LEGO  (optional)  
   • Define color tables (COLO) and legend entries (LEGO) per‐picture.

10. AND  (position override)  
   • Forces the next plot into a specific sub‐box by number or literal code.  
   • Can reset page or continue on same sheet.

11. Coordinate‐dimension settings  
   • “Dimensional line” flag: “–” no dims, “=” draw coordinates.  
   • Planes:  
     – YZ: dim on Y–Z plane.  
     – ZX: Z–X.  
     – XY: X–Y.  
   • Two‐axis dimensioning alternative to default “picture coordinates.”  
   • Observer‐view must be set with VIEW to achieve desired reduction scale.  
   • GRAPHIC chooses which axis to place vertically/horizontally by vertical‐extent size.

Usage notes:  
– If TYPE is an ANSI/HP code, standard inner/external margins are automatically set; URS suppresses external margins altogether.  
– STAN shifts the header band to align HEAD lines; ZTVK creates title bands top and bottom.  
– Subdivision lets multiple plots share one sheet; AND can jump to any cell.  
– Each plot gets its own legend whose height is controlled by SLEG, with internal text heights by SCHH.  
– By default the coordinate axes, grid scale, a 1 cm sample line, and dimensional lines appear within the inner border.  

This meta‐structure gives a complete picture of how page size, orientation, scaling, margins, subdivision and legend/head‐block parameters are defined via the SIZ2 (and related) records in SOFiSTiK/GRAPHIC.

The table defines two configuration parameters—SPLI and SLEG—used when subdividing a drawing sheet into multiple “pictures” (plots) and allocating space for their legends. It is typically part of the SIZ2 record in the GRAPHIC/SOFISTIK RAG (Retrieve–Augment–Generate) workflow. Below is a breakdown of its structure and semantics:

1. Table Structure  
   • Columns  
     – Item: the keyword or record name.  
     – Description: a brief explanation of what the parameter does. In the case of SPLI it also shows the two literal‐syntax variants.  
     – Unit: the measurement or data type expected.  
     – Default: the value assumed if the user does not explicitly supply one.

2. Parameter: SPLI  
   • Item name: SPLI  
   • Purpose: Defines how the paper is partitioned into a grid of sub‐plots and in which sequence they are filled. When you want to produce multiple “little pictures” on one sheet, you set SPLI to specify the number of rows and columns and the fill order.  
   • Syntax variants (entered as a literal, “LIT”):  
     – heightXwidth (uppercase X)  
       • Creates a grid of “height” rows and “width” columns  
       • Fills column by column (i.e. first fills all rows in column 1, then column 2, etc.)  
     – height*width (asterisk)  
       • Creates the same grid dimensions  
       • Fills row by row (i.e. first fills all columns in row 1, then row 2, etc.)  
   • Unit: LIT (literal string combining two integers with either “X” or “*”)  
   • Default: “1*1”  
     – Implies a single cell (one row, one column) with row‐by‐row filling (irrelevant for a 1×1 case).

3. Parameter: SLEG  
   • Item name: SLEG  
   • Purpose: Specifies the vertical height of each subplot’s legend area (sometimes called the “partial legend”) within the inner margin of its grid cell. This controls how much space, in millimeters or centimeters, is reserved under the graphic for the legend text.  
   • Unit: cm  
   • Default: 1.5 cm  
     – Provides a modest area for one or two lines of legend. If you subdivide the sheet into many small plots, you can reduce SLEG or adjust text heights (via SCHH/H1 or HLEG) to fit more entries.

4. Usage Context  
   • These two parameters are invoked after you choose paper format and scale with SIZE or SIZ2 and before issuing AND (to jump to a particular cell) or before plotting.  
   • Typical workflow:  
     1. Call SIZE to set paper type, margins, orientation.  
     2. Use SIZ2 to subdivide via SPLI and set legend height via SLEG.  
     3. Optionally use AND to select which grid cell to plot in.  
     4. Issue DRAW commands (plotted structure, axes, grid, etc.).  
     5. Move to next cell automatically or explicitly.  
   • Together, SPLI and SLEG give you fine control over multi‐plot layouts on a single sheet—number of panels, fill order, and legend spacing—critical for engineering drawings, results comparisons, or diagram collections.

The figure is a black-and-white, two-panel illustration demonstrating how the GRAPHIC “STAN” paper partitioning (SIZ2) allocates external margins, inner margins, title bands and plot area. A heavy outer rectangle defines the full sheet (external margin). Inside it, two adjacent sub-frames (left and right) are separated by a shaded vertical strip (the inner margin displaced by STAN so that HEAD lines fall between inner and external margins). Across the very top of the sheet runs a header band: on the left of the band is the text “GRAF 12294 26.05.95,” in the center “Katz + Bellmann,” and on the right a postal address and telephone number. Below the two panels, outside the outer rectangle, is a thick baseline carrying the caption “Figure 3.1: Partitioning of the drawing paper STAN.”

Left Panel  
• Sub-frame: simple three-segment “⌜⌟” shape (a U-shaped structure) drawn in medium-weight lines.  
• Nodes labeled “1” at the bottom of the left vertical leg, “2” at the midpoint of the top horizontal leg, and “3” at the bottom of the right vertical leg.  
• Along the bottom of the plot area is a straight horizontal “scale” line with tick marks labeled 1.00, 2.00, 3.00, 4.00, 5.00. This indicates the “picture coordinates” grid.  
• On the left margin, a vertical arrow points inward and is captioned “HLEG” – this denotes the user-definable legend/title band height.  
• Beneath the left plot, two small dimension lines labeled “Textheight H1” and “Textheight H0” show the two SCHH parameters controlling the HEAD (title) and picture-legend text sizes.

Right Panel  
• Sub-frame: a four-segment rectangular “⌜⌟” loop. The four corner nodes are labeled sequentially “1” (lower left), “2” (upper left), “3” (upper right) and “4” (lower right).  
• A vertical coordinate axis with tick marks and numeric labels (e.g. –4.00 near the top, –2.00 mid-span, 0.00 at plot bottom) is drawn just to the left of the plot, illustrating that STAN can also dimension two selected axes instead of only picture coordinates.  
• Beneath the right plot runs another scaled baseline identical to the left panel (1.00 … 5.00).  
• To the right of the right panel, a thin arrow labeled “WLEG” points to the bottom legend band and indicates the width of the right margin as controlled by the WLEG parameter.

Overall Notes  
• The thin inner margin (shaded) is automatically set so that the HEAD lines (first GRAPHIC HEAD line for structure name, subsequent HEAD lines for building part, bar line, event line, etc.) fall between the inner and outer margins.  
• The bottom border (default ~1.0 cm high) is used for HEAD lines or picture legend controlled by HLEG (can be increased or decreased and text size adjusted via SCHH H1 or H10 or legend HLEG/SLEG).  
• The external margin is omitted only with single-paper printers or TYPE URS.  
• By assigning TYPE STAN or using SIZ2 entries, the program chooses an ANSI/DIN/American/HP plotter paper size, orientation (minus sign for portrait), and places the plot area between upper and lower title bands (or on the right side for larger drawings).  
• Plot subdivision (height × width grid) and explicit positioning via record AND are possible; a new paper requires a fresh SIZE or SIZ2 input.

The image is a black-and-white line drawing illustrating the “ZTVK” title-band layout on a single sheet (for example, DIN-A4 portrait).  It is composed of three nested rectangles representing, from outside in, the paper limit (external margin), the printable area (inner margin), and the actual plot region.  Within the printable area, two horizontal “title bands” are shown: one at the very top edge of the plotting rectangle and one (implicitly) at the bottom (though only the upper band is explicitly populated in this figure).

At the upper title band, aligned flush against the left inner margin, there are three labelled fields:  
  • “BUILDING PART:” followed by the text “Bauteil, Wurzelplatte”  
  • “BLOCK:” followed by “Blockbeschreibung”  
  • “VVORANG :” (appearing as a field header with its trailing colon, but no content to its right)

Each of these labels uses an all-caps font for the field name (“BUILDING PART,” “BLOCK,” “VVORANG”) followed by a colon, and a normal-weight text string for the field value.  The text strings seem to be German domain terminology (“Bauteil” = component, “Wurzelplatte” = base plate, etc.), suggesting that the structure’s identity and description are recorded here.

Below these data fields—and still inside the inner margin—a small two-axis coordinate symbol is drawn in the lower-left corner of the plotting rectangle:  
  • A horizontal arrow pointing to the right, labelled “X” at its tip  
  • A vertical arrow pointing upward, labelled “Y” at its tip  

These axes denote the orientation of the global coordinate system for the drawing that would appear in the main plot area (which is left blank in this figure for demonstration of the title-band format only).

Outside the drawing itself, centered beneath the lower edge of the external margin, is the caption text “Figure 3.2: ZTVK title bands.”  This caption is set in a bold or heavier weight font compared to the field labels, indicating it is the figure title.  

Overall, the figure demonstrates how the ZTVK command generates standardized title bands—with fields for structural part name, block description, and revision; spacing dictated by inner and outer margins; and a built-in coordinate-axis legend—around the actual graphical content.  The crisp rectangular frames and alignment of text show the precise engineering-drawing conventions (DIN/ISO format) enforced by the program, including consistent margin widths and designated zones for header lines that can be further customized (text height, number of lines, placement left or right on larger sheets, etc.).

The illustration is a two-panel diagram labeled “Figure 3.3: Partitioning of the drawing sheet ZTVK TYPE 4 and 3.” Each panel shows how a technical drawing sheet is subdivided into coordinate plots, title bands, margins, and grid cells with sequential numbering. Below is a detailed breakdown:

1. Overall Layout  
   • Two rectangles represent full drawing sheets. Inside each, a heavy border marks the outer paper margin. Within that lies a thinner inner border indicating the printable area.  
   • Title bands (HEAD lines) appear as shaded horizontal strips. On the left panel (TYPE 4) they run along the top and bottom edges; on the right panel (TYPE 3), the top band shifts to the right side of the sheet (portrait orientation for the title on a larger format).  
   • At the very bottom of each sheet is a narrow margin reserved for legends and user/program information. In the TYPE 4 view this bottom band is larger and contains a boxed legend area at the right.  

2. Left Panel (ZTVK TYPE 4 – smaller format)  
   • Inner border margins are set approximately 0.5 cm from the outer border. The top margin houses two thin header lines; the bottom margin includes a legend block of about 1.0 cm in height on the right side.  
   • The plot area is a stepped grid of 8 columns by 7 rows (with the lower-left corner missing two cells, giving an “L” shape).  
   • Grid lines are drawn in thin, evenly spaced strokes; major grid intersection points are marked with small filled circles.  
   • Inside each cell is a sequential two-digit label: starting at “13” in the upper left, then “14,” “25,” “26,” “37,” “38,” etc., proceeding row by row down and to the right. The last few cells are numbered “103,” “104,” “115,” “116.”  
   • Along the bottom of the plot area a horizontal scale is shown with tick marks at 0.00, 5.00, 10.00. The units appear in meters.  
   • On the right side of the inner border vertical dimension ticks mark off distances at 5.00 and 10.00, indicating the height of the plot.  

3. Right Panel (ZTVK TYPE 3 – larger format)  
   • A similar stepped grid appears but occupies a larger printable region. This format omits the bottom legend block and instead places title bands along the right edge (portrait placement of HEAD lines).  
   • The grid here is 10 columns by 8 rows (again with an L-shaped removal of two lower-left cells). Major intersections carry filled circles.  
   • Cell numbering mirrors the left panel’s pattern but continues to higher numbers (e.g. “79,” “80,” “91,” “92,” up to “118”).  
   • Coordinate axes and scale labels (0.00, 5.00, 10.00) repeat at the bottom, while the right side shows vertical dimension markers identical to the left layout.  
   • The heavier outer borders and more generous margins reflect the larger SIZE and the different FORM settings for an ANSI or HP paper type.  

4. Key Graphic Elements  
   • Outer margin (external) shown as the thickest line; inner margin as a thin line inset roughly 0.5 cm.  
   • Title bands/HEAD lines appear as blank bands but are captioned in the context text with parameters HLEG, H1, H10.  
   • Coordinate grid lines subdivide the plot; major intersections indicated.  
   • Dimension ticks with numeric labels along the axes mark the global origin at (0.00, 0.00).  
   • The numbering inside cells corresponds to a “heightxwidth” partitioning literal—here 7×8 for TYPE 4 and 8×10 for TYPE 3—demonstrating the AND record’s ability to position multiple subplots.  

Together, the two panels visualize how the GRAPHIC system’s SIZ2, TYPE, W, H, SC, AND and related records control paper size, orientation, margins, title band placement, and automatic grid partitioning for multi-plot technical drawings.

The figure shows a schematic view of how a ZTVK TYPE 2 drawing sheet is partitioned into a regular grid of subplots, complete with axes, node markers and a reserved title/legend area. At its core, the drawing area is laid out as an L-shaped network of square cells, each cell framed by thin grid lines meeting in small circular “node” markers at every corner. The horizontal extent of the grid runs from an origin at 0.00 (on the lower left corner of the full rectangle) to 15.00 units on the right. Vertically it extends from 0.00 at the lower boundary up to 10.00 units at the top, though the grid itself is omitted in the lower left quadrant to form the L-shape.

Starting near the upper left area, two adjacent squares are marked “13” and “14.” Directly beneath them, another pair is labeled “25” and “26,” followed in subsequent rows by “37” & “38,” “49” & “50,” and “61” & “62.” In the central inward notch of the L, a similar 2×2 block carries “79” & “80” on its first row, and “91” & “92” immediately below. Adjacent to that, two more cells are marked “103” & “104” and beneath them “115” & “116.” These numbered blocks illustrate how the AND record or literal “height×width” notation might map subplots onto particular grid positions when subdividing the sheet.  

Beyond the grid, the rightmost 2-unit-wide strip is reserved for title bands, legends or metadata. About halfway up this margin, two thin horizontal rectangles appear stacked: these are likely reserved for header lines or additional annotations. Alongside this, the vertical axis is repeated with tick marks at 0.00, 5.00 and 10.00 units to provide a clear scale reference even within the margin area. At the very bottom right corner, a larger, empty rectangular block denotes the main legend box (its height is controlled by the SLEG or HLEG parameters).

Just below that, the caption “Figure 3.4: Partitioning of the drawing sheet ZTVK TYPE 2” is centered. The combination of bold-outlined numbered cells, thin grid lines, node markers, axis scales and dedicated margins reflects the graphic system’s rules for automatic paper-size selection, margin allocation (inner and external), subdivision of plots, and placement of title bands and legends as described in the surrounding specification text.

The table defines a set of layout and formatting parameters used by the SOFiMSHA/REPORT-BROWSER framework to control how structures, legends, borders, spacing, and auxiliary text (date, HEAD lines) are rendered on output sheets or in browser‐driven picture downloads.  Each row consists of:

• Item  
• Description (semantic meaning and allowed values)  
• Unit (LIT = literal, cm = centimeters, “–” = dimensionless factor)  
• Default (used when no explicit setting is provided)

Below is a detailed walk-through of each parameter and how it affects the final output:

1. UMBR (Unit = LIT; Default = YES)  
   – Controls automatic line wrapping in the picture legend.  
     • NO  no line breaks at all  
     • YES inserts a break only if a legend line exceeds the available width  
     • SUPP breaks at the next blank space when line too long  
     • SHOR forces a break even inside a long uninterrupted word  

2. DRUU / DRUR / DRUL / DRUD (Unit = cm; Default = 0.5 each)  
   – Define the margins (print borders) around the structure or picture:  
     • DRUU = upper border thickness  
     • DRUR = right border  
     • DRUL = left border  
     • DRUD = lower border  

3. LEGW (Unit = cm; Default = “*”)  
   – Width of the legend when it is embedded directly within a picture.  
     An asterisk (*) denotes “automatic” sizing based on content or downstream defaults.

4. FREE (Unit = cm; Default = 0.2)  
   – Minimum clear space to leave around the structure graphics.  
     • If FREE ≥ 0.0 cm, additional axes or annotations are included within that margin.  
     • If FREE < 0.0 cm, that absolute value is used strictly as the gap, ignoring axes.

5. FAKH (Unit = —; Default = 0.5)  
   – Vertical spacing between successive legend lines, expressed as a multiple of the text height.  
     • The base text height is defined by SCHH H10 (see “See also: SCHH”).  

6. SHAE (Unit = LIT; Default = YES)  
   – Governs representation of the HEAD line (structure identifier line) produced by SOFiMSHA.  
     • NO  suppress HEAD line entirely  
     • YES include HEAD line in the sheet legend; if the sheet’s database differs from the current one, it is placed in the picture legend along with the database path  
     • OR any literal combination (up to 4 characters) drawn from:  
       – P = always write full path (even if database is available)  
       – C = separate structure line and path onto two lines (or combine if space allows)  
       – H = write only the structure line (no path)  
       – A = write the complete absolute database‐file path  
       – R = write the relative path from the input file location  
       – N = write only the database file name  
     • Note: A, R, and N are mutually exclusive.  

7. DATE (Unit = LIT; Default = YES)  
   – Toggles printing of the current date within the sheet’s frame.  
     • NO omit date  
     • YES print date  

8. SPLI (Unit = LIT; Default = “*”)  
   – Defines picture positioning behavior in the REPORT-BROWSER. It works in tandem with SIZ2:  
     • SIZ2 SPLI PICT (default when browser supports REPORT-BROWSER)  
       – Generates individual picture files; the browser places each on the sheet at a fixed size (set by SIZE SPLI). Values in the AND record are ignored for picture sizing.  
     • SIZ2 SPLI PAGE  
       – Stores full pages (all pictures laid out together). Picture dimensions and placement may vary; list lengths are limited by the picture size.  

See also:  
• SIZE (defines global picture size for REPORT-BROWSER)  
• SCHH (text height definitions, e.g. H10)  
• COLO, LEGO (color and legend grouping settings)  
• AND (additional settings that may affect picture sizing)  
• DB (database file references and overrides)  
• SIZ2 (mode switch between single‐PICTURE vs. full‐PAGE output)

Together, these parameters give fine-grained control over margins, legend formatting, HEAD-line inclusion, date stamping, and picture‐placement logic when generating chemical or structural drawings in sheets or browser‐based reports.

 The item SHAE controls the output of the line of the structure defined with the program SOFiMSHA. The line of the structure is printed as a default in the sheet legend, if the same database is used at this sheet. In case of different databases the line of the structure is placed in the picture legend with the complete path of the database file. This can be controlled with a literal combination of the following characters (maximal 4). In this case ”A” and ”R” exclude each other:
 P The line of the structure or the path are written always into the picture (also if the database is available).
 C The line of the structure and the path (if it is requested) are placed in different lines, else, if the place is sufficient, together in one line.
 H Only the line of the structure is written.
 A Only the complete path for the database file is written.
 R Only the relative path with reference to the position of the input file is writ- ten.
 N Only the database file name is written.
 The parameter ”A”, ””R” and ”N” are mutually exclusive.
 The picture-positioning in the browser REPORT BROWSER is defined with the item SPLI. With the input SIZ2 SPLI PICT (default if the browser REPORT BROWSER is supported) single pictures are created. The browser REPORT BROWSER is placing this pictures on the sheet. This is the correct way to mixing pictures and lists. Pictures have a fixed defined size depending on SIZE SPLI. The input values to pictures size in the record AND are ignored. With the input SIZ2 SPLI PAGE (default if the browser REPORT BROWSER is supported) always the complete page including all pictures is stored. Pictures may have varying sizes and placements. The length of lists are limited on the size of the picture.

content:
The table defines a small command-set for controlling how individual “pictures” (drawing areas) are placed, sized and scaled on a sheet.  These commands typically follow structural or load-definition inputs (e.g. STRU, LOAD, NODE, BEAM, QUAD, ISOL, SECT) and work in concert with the logic for new sheets vs. layered drawings (the AND‐logic described in your context).  Below is a detailed breakdown of each item, its role, units and default behavior:

1. POSI  
   • Purpose: selects or creates an entry in the current sheet’s picture list.  It also lets you jump back to an already-defined picture by number.  
   • Unit: none ( — )  
   • Default: “*” (asterisk) – automatically uses the next available picture index in the list.  
   • Context: if no AND input has appeared, a non-AND record always starts a new sheet and implicitly increments POSI.  If you supply AND, you continue adding layers to the last referenced POSI.

2. POSL, POSR, POSD, POSU  
   • Purpose: define the bounding rectangle of the picture within the sheet’s graphic area as percentages.  
     – POSL (left border)  
     – POSR (right border)  
     – POSD (lower border)  
     – POSU (upper border)  
   • Units: percent (%) of the overall graphic area.  
   • Defaults:  
     – POSL = 0 (left aligned)  
     – POSR = 100 (extend to right edge)  
     – POSD = 0 (bottom aligned)  
     – POSU = 100 (extend to top edge)  
   • Notes: once the first layer is drawn and the picture size is fixed, these borders cannot be changed thereafter.  Pictures should be at least 1 × 1 cm.

3. SC  (Scale control)  
   • Purpose: sets the drawing scale for all layers in the current picture.  
   • Unit: dimensionless or library units (–/LIT)  
   • Default: DEFA  
   • Valid values:  
     – A positive numeric “value” – the system attempts to use exactly that scale; if the requested scale would clip content, it selects the closest fit.  A safety check is skipped if “value” × 1E+10 is used.  
     – DEFA – automatic “engineering scale” chosen to best fill the defined picture area.  
     – 0 – forces “picture filling” mode, i.e. maximize content to fill the box.  
   • Interaction: SC is evaluated after POSL/POSR/POSD/POSU define the picture size.  It remains constant for all subsequent AND-layers until a new SC or new picture is defined.

4. MSCA (Scale determination mode)  
   • Purpose: controls how bounding boxes (system boxes) and any outlying representations are measured when computing or validating scale.  
   • Unit: literal selection (LIT)  
   • Default: FULL  
   • Options:  
     – NO – only the system box of the first layer is considered.  
     – REPR – same as NO, but also include any geometry in layer 1 that lies outside its system box.  
     – ALL – use the system boxes of every layer (but ignore outlying geometry).  
     – FULL – consider both system boxes and all outlying geometry across all layers.  
   • When to use: MSCA NO is fastest (scans only one box), but may clip later layers.  MSCA FULL ensures nothing is lost but requires an extra pre-scan of every layer.

How these items tie in with layering (AND) and sheets:  
• The first record without AND starts a new sheet and creates picture 1 with POSI=* (or explicit).  
• Each subsequent record lacking AND also starts a new sheet/picture.  
• Records prefixed by AND refer back to the most recently active POSI, adding extra drawing layers at the same position/scale.  
• A sheet can contain up to 64 pictures.  POSI lets you switch between them freely.  POSL/POSR/POSD/POSU lock in each picture’s viewport, while SC and MSCA ensure the content is scaled and clipped (or not) according to your requirements.

See also: STRU, LOAD, NODE, BEAM, QUAD, ISOL, SECT
 AND
 If AND is not input, the next drawing is represented always at a new sheet. If several pictures are at one sheet, the next drawing is printed in the next picture position.
 An input for AND represents the next drawing order (layer) in the same picture. If no further inputs for AND occur, this layer is assigned to the at last processed picture. The scale remains unchanged.
 It is changed to the new picture or a picture not defined yet is generated, if the record AND contains further inputs.
 The current sheet obtains the list of the defined pictures from the previous sheet, that is their positioning at the sheet. One can jump to a picture of this list with POSI. The current position
 is the default for POSI. Maximal 64 pictures per sheet are possible.
 The position of a picture at a sheet can be defined freely within a graphic area with inputs for POSL, POSR, POSD and POSU. However, the picture should not be selected smaller than 1x1 cm. The size of the picture is defined in the first drawing. Then it can not be changed anymore.
 The scale which is calculated for the picture depends on the size of the structure box (system box) and the width of the borders around this box. The calculation is fastest, if the first layer of a picture with its structure is considered only in each case (MSCA NO). MSCA FULL should be input to prevent that representations are outside the picture. The entire picture is scanned to representations outside the picture and then the scale is adapted before the real drawing.

The table is organized into four columns—Item, Description, Unit, Default—and enumerates a series of “H-” parameters, miscellaneous size- and legend-related controls, plus two overlap-checking settings (REVI, TREV). Together these inputs govern text and symbol sizing, legend layout, dimensional-line scales, and collision-avoidance logic in SOFiSTiK graphical output. Below is a detailed breakdown:

1. Column Definitions  
   • Item: Parameter name or code  
   • Description: What the parameter controls  
   • Unit: Measurement unit (cm, %, LIT, or “–” when unitless)  
   • Default: Factory setting if unspecified  

2. Heading and Legend Parameters (H1–H8)  
   • H1 (cm, default = *): Overall legend height or width  
     – Positive value: explicit definition  
     – Negative value: auto-adapt to legend width  
   • H2 (cm, default = 0.25): Text line spacing in the top border  
   • H3, H4: Marked “obsolete,” formerly reserved for other border text  
   • H5 (cm, default = 0.20): Scale of dimensional lines (unit = 1001 SOFiSTiK-Units)  
   • H6 (cm, default = 0.16): Height of “Results” label text  
   • H7: Obsolete  
   • H8 (cm, default = 0.20): FILL scale for the left-hand border  

3. Symbol and Text-Width Factors  
   • HS (cm, default = 0.35): Size factor for spring symbols in side views  
   • MS: Obsolete (formerly a marker size)  
   • FACW (–, default = 0.70): Width factor for result text, relative to text height  

4. Overlap-Checking: REVI (Allowed overlapping for texts)  
   • Unit = %; default = EXTR (5 %)  
   • Options:  
     – NO: no overlap check  
     – YES: allow up to 40 % overlap  
     – FULL: allow up to 25 % overlap  
     – EXTR: allow up to 5 % overlap  
     – 0…100: specify custom percent threshold  
   • Mechanism: divides sheet into a 0.7 mm grid; lettering is allocated grid cells; if overlap percent exceeds limit, new labels are omitted or selected per TREV setting.  

5. Obsolete and Auxiliary Items  
   • MINH, MINW: Obsolete entries for minimum heights/widths  
   • H10 (cm, default = H1): Text height of a partial legend—if zero, legend text is omitted  
   • FACS (–, default = 0.80): Text-width factor for partial legends  

6. Overlap-Checking Type: TREV  
   • Unit = LIT (literal keywords); default = AMAX  
   • Defines how to compute overlap metrics:  
     – FIRS: ignore following values  
     – MINV: use the smaller of conflicting values  
     – MAXV: use the larger value in foreground  
     – AMIN: use absolute smaller values  
     – AMAX: use absolute larger values  

Additional Context (from accompanying text):  
• Zero text sizes suppress corresponding designations, especially helpful for inner-border lines and FILL scales.  
• All numeric outputs (graph, legend, lists) adhere to decimal-place rules set by ND:  
  – NDIM bases decimals on unit settings  
  – NMAX tailors decimals to value magnitude (values >1 E+7 use exponential format)  
• REVI’s grid-based overlap test excludes certain element types (CURV, TEXT, NIVE, POST, AXIS).  
• More exact overlap checks (higher REVI precision) require more processing time.

Below is a conceptual, field‐by‐field breakdown of the “continued” table, geared toward ingestion into a RAG‐style vector store.  It combines the visible layout hints with the surrounding SOFiSTiK‐manual context so that each cell or parameter can be indexed, embedded and retrieved effectively.

1. Table Scope & Purpose  
   • Purpose: Defines graphical‐output parameters (text sizes, scales, units, display rules) for three-dimensional line representations in SOFiSTiK plots.  
   • Continuation: This segment picks up mid-stream (see “Table continued on next page”), so it inherits earlier column headings such as “Parameter,” “Abbrev.,” “Value,” “Unit,” “Display Condition,” “Default,” “Notes.”

2. Columns (Inferred)  
   1. Parameter (Full name)  
      – e.g. SCHH, AMAX, MAXZ, MINV, AMIN, ND, NMAX, REVI, TREV  
      – Text: plain string  
   2. Abbrev. / Code  
      – Short code used in input decks (e.g. “SCH2,” “SIZE,” “COLB”)  
      – Text  
   3. Value / Setting  
      – Numeric or special flag: >0, =0, <0 or explicit text size (e.g. “0,” “2.5,” “1E+7”)  
      – Data type: integer or real  
   4. Unit  
      – Most dimensional lines: SOFiSTiK-Unit 1001  
      – Legend or scale: unitless or according to “FILL scale”  
      – Text  
   5. Display Condition  
      – “> 0” → always show  
      – “= 0” → suppress designation  
      – “< 0” → only show when sign changes (for legend entries)  
      – Text with logical operator  
   6. Default  
      – Built-in default if omitted (e.g. default ND decimal places, default INTE SET 9 PAR1 =1.E+7 for E-format threshold)  
      – Numeric/text  
   7. Notes / Comments  
      – References to related commands (SCH2, SCH3, LEGO, COLB)  
      – Behavior notes (e.g., zero text size omits labels, applies to inner border lines)  
      – Formatting rules (decimal rounding via ND, exponential format for large values)  
      – Overlap‐avoidance via REVI/TREV grid logic  

3. Row-Level Semantics  
   • Each row ties a graphic element (dimension line, border fill, legend item, axis designation) to:  
     – a code (how the user invokes it in the SOFiSTiK input),  
     – a numeric/text setting,  
     – the drawing unit,  
     – a simple display rule,  
     – and any inter-parameter dependencies.  
   • Example row (hypothetical reconstruction):  
     Parameter: “Inner Border Text Size” | Abbrev: “SCHH” | Value: “0” | Unit: “1001” | Display: “=0” (omit) | Default: “1.0” | Note: “Zero suppresses labels on inner border.”

4. Cross-References & Dependencies  
   • See also SCH2, SCH3, SIZE, LEGO, COLB – these likely control other graphic elements and share the “text‐size/scale/display” pattern.  
   • ND family (NDIM vs. NMAX) dictates decimal‐place rules; “INTE SET 9 PAR1” threshold triggers E-format.  
   • REVI/TREV govern automatic label‐overlap prevention:  
     – Paper is gridded at 0.7 mm increments.  
     – Each text occupies grid cells; overlap fraction is specified as a percentage.  
     – If overlap > threshold, the later label is either skipped or replaced, per TREV input.

5. Formatting & Rounding Rules  
   • All numeric outputs in graph, legend, list adhere to ND‐controlled decimal places.  
   • ND NMAX auto‐scales precision by value magnitude; ND NDIM ties precision to unit definitions.  
   • Values below the smallest representable unit show as “0.0” (signed if needed).  
   • Values exceeding INTE SET 9 PAR1 (default 1.E+7) display in E (scientific) notation.

6. Recommended Vector-Store Schema  
   – id: composite key (Parameter code + Abbrev)  
   – parameter_name: full name  
   – code: invocation string  
   – value: numeric or flag  
   – unit: text  
   – display_condition: enumeration {“always”, “never”, “if_sign_change”}  
   – default_value: numeric/text  
   – notes: free text with cross‐refs and special rules  
   – related_commands: list [SCH2, SCH3, …]  
   – precision_rule: reference to ND setting  
   – overlap_logic: reference to REVI/TREV grid rule

By capturing the table in this structured fashion—mapping each cell to a typed field with clear semantic labels—you ensure robust retrieval, contextual linking (e.g. “which parameters obey ND rounding?”), and straightforward embedding in a RAG pipeline.

The table is organized in four columns—Item, Description, Unit and Default—and defines a set of control parameters for formatting and overlapping of text and extremal values in SOFiSTiK graphical output. Below is a detailed breakdown of each parameter and its purpose:

1. ND  
   • Description: Number of decimal places displayed after the comma.  
     – NMAX: Decide decimals based on the maximum value.  
     – NDIM: Use the decimal‐place convention of the SOFiSTiK units.  
     – 99: Force exponential (E) format.  
     – 0…9: Explicit number of decimal digits.  
   • Unit: LIT/–  
   • Default: NDIM  
   • Notes:  
     – All graph, legend and list outputs use the number of decimal places specified here.  
     – Values smaller than the smallest representable digit show as “0.0” (with sign if needed).  
     – Values exceeding the INTE SET 9 PAR1 threshold (default 1.E+7) appear in E format.

2. REVX and REVY  
   • Description: Edge‐distance threshold for allowing text overlap, given as a factor of the text size in the X (horizontal) or Y (vertical) direction.  
   • Unit: –  
   • Default: 0.33  

3. RMIN  
   • Description: Minimum permitted distance for text overlap.  
   • Unit: cm  
   • Default: 0.0  

4. RMAX  
   • Description: Maximum permitted distance for text overlap.  
   • Unit: cm  
   • Default: 1.0  

5. RMOD  
   • Description: Selection of text‐overlapping rules.  
     – ALL: Enable all overlap checks.  
     – DIM: Ignore unit‐based checks.  
     – DIR: Ignore directional checks.  
     – NO: Disable all overlap checks.  
   • Unit: LIT  
   • Default: ALL  

6. RTOL  
   • Description: Angular tolerance (0…90°) within which directional overlap is permitted.  
   • Unit: grad  
   • Default: 15  

7. MAXX  
   • Description: Method of checking and displaying maximum values, using the same literal scheme as the TREV input for text overlap.  
     – DEFA: Apply current text‐overlap (TREV) settings.  
   • Unit: LIT  
   • Default: MAXV  

8. MMOD  
   • Description: Parameters governing the treatment of maximum values, analogous to RMOD for text.  
     – OFF: Suppress maximum‐value display entirely.  
     – DEFA: Use current text‐overlapping settings (RMOD).  
   • Unit: LIT  
   • Default: RIC  

9. MAXN  
   • Description: Count of maximum (MAXV or AMAX) or minimum (MINV or AMIN) values to show per direction and per unit.  
     –  >0: Always show that many extrema.  
     –  =0: Do not show any.  
     –  <0: Show only if the sign changes (e.g. from positive to negative).  
   • Unit: –  
   • Default: 1  

10. MINN  
    • Description: Same as MAXN but for minimum values if MINV/AMIN or maximum values if MINV/AMIN applies contrariwise.  
    • Unit: –  
    • Default: –1  

Additional Context from the Extended Text:  
– If a text size is set to zero, the corresponding textual designation (e.g. dimension lines on an inner border, or the FILL‐scale label) is entirely omitted. Dimension lines use SOFiSTiK unit 1001 and refer to the optical 3D projection plane perpendicular to the line of sight.  
– Global formatting rules (>0 always displayed; =0 never; <0 only on sign change) apply to both MAXN and MINN.  
– To avoid overcrowding, REVI (or TREV) can be used: a grid is imposed on the paper (0.7 mm spacing), text blocks “occupy” grid cells, and any candidate overlap beyond a specified percentage is either removed or retained based on the TREV setting. This check excludes additional designations like CURV, TEXT, NIVE, POST and AXIS and may increase processing time if performed at higher precision.

The fragment you provided appears to be the continuation of a multi-page parameter table (likely for the SOFiSTiK “SET GRAPH” or similar module).  It defines a handful of sub-parameters, their allowable values or switches, and the way they influence drawing and labeling.  Below is a structured description of each entry in that continuation:

1. SCHH  
   – A sub-setting of the SCH(ema) family (see also SCH2, SCH3) that controls the height or placement of the schema heading in the plot.  
   – Its exact numeric range isn’t shown here, but it nests under general SIZE, LEGO and COLB parameters, which govern text size, legend geometry, and color blocks.

2. AMAX  
   – When activated, the system picks “absolute maximum” values for each direction and unit.  
   – I.e. if you have both positive and negative results in a given plotting direction, AMAX forces the display of whichever has the larger magnitude, regardless of sign.

3. MAXZ  
   – In contrast, MAXZ always uses the values that lie in front (foreground) in a 3D sense.  
   – This can be useful when you want the topmost (in Z-direction) result rather than the mathematically largest.

4. MINV / AMIN  
   – These switches work similarly for minima:  
     • MINV picks the smallest plotted values in each direction.  
     • AMIN picks the minimum by absolute magnitude.  

5. Sign-dependency for showing values  
   – A simple three-state rule:  
     • “> 0”  – always show the numerical annotation.  
     • “= 0”  – suppress display entirely.  
     • “< 0”  – show only when a change of sign occurs (e.g. at a zero crossing, as in legends).

6. Zero text-size omission  
   – If any text-size parameter is explicitly set to zero, its entire annotation is omitted.  
   – Common use cases:  
     • Dimension lines of the inner border.  
     • The “FILL” scale bar along the left margin.  
   – Dimension lines themselves use SOFiSTiK‐unit code 1001 and always lie in the optical plane perpendicular to the view direction.

7. Decimal‐place control via ND  
   – All plotted values, legend entries and list outputs adhere to the ND setting:  
     • ND NDIM – number of decimals follows the underlying SOFiSTiK‐unit definitions.  
     • ND NMAX – decimals vary with the size of the number (see also INTE SET 9).  
   – Rounding:  
     • Very small values that round below the display precision become “0.0” (with sign if needed).  
     • Very large values (≥ INTE SET 9 PAR1, default 1.0E+7) appear in exponential (E) format.

8. Overlapping‐label prevention (REVI / TREV)  
   – The paper is overlaid with a grid of 0.7 mm cells. Each label claims one or more cells.  
   – A tolerance percentage (input parameter) defines how much two labels may overlap (re-use the same grid cells).  
   – If the overlap exceeds that threshold, the label is either removed or repositioned according to the TREV setting.  
   – Note: More stringent (lower‐threshold) checks cost extra computation time.  
   – REVI/TREV do not apply to the “always‐present” element labels (CURV, TEXT, NIVE, POST, AXIS).

This completes the table’s continuation.  Each parameter fine-tunes how data values and annotations appear in your graphical output—whether by choosing which extremum to plot, how many decimals to show, or how to avoid clutter by suppressing or repositioning overlapping text.

Below is a structured, natural-language “walk-through” of the three parameters shown in your screenshot, explaining how they fit into the overall SOFiSTiK graphic‐output scheme (see also SCH2, SCH3, SIZE, LEGO, COLB and the notes on SCHH, AMAX/MINV/AMIN, ND, REVI/TREV).

1. Table structure  
   • Column 1 “Item”: the keyword you enter in your input deck.  
   • Column 2 “Description”: what the keyword does and any special flags or sub-options.  
   • Column 3 “Unit”: the data type or unit the keyword expects (if none, a dash “–”).  
   • Column 4 “Default”: the value SOFiSTiK will use if you don’t specify this keyword.

2. MAXR – “Other foreground colour for maximum values”  
   • Purpose: overrides the normal text/line colour used when plotting a maximum value in a graph.  
   • How it works: internally it references the COLO record (your RGB or palette index table).  
   • Special flags:  
     – add +16000 if you want the override to apply only to the “edge” of the text or frame.  
     – add +32000 + (colour index + 1) if you want a different colour for negative-valued maxima.  
   • Unit: – (no numeric unit).  
   • Default: 1001 (i.e. the built-in “highlight” colour index).

3. MAXF – “Other background colour for maximum values”  
   • Purpose: sets a fill or background colour behind the maximum value annotation.  
   • Details: again uses the COLO record to look up an RGB index. By convention, index 15 is light-grey.  
   • Unit: –  
   • Default: –1 (i.e. no background fill unless you explicitly choose a non-negative colour index).

4. MPRP – “Additional markings of maximum values”  
   • Purpose: control whether and how extra symbology appears next to each maximum. You supply a literal string consisting of any combination of the following letters:  
     R   Draw a frame around the maximum value. (If you also set MAXR line-width > 0, you get a specially bold frame.)  
     T   Print additional text (for example “MAX=”) before the number. The text itself comes from the SCHH record (the “WING” text item).  
     N   Suppress the printing of the numeric maximum-value itself.  
     L   Suppress the printing of the maximum load value (if plotting loads rather than displacements or stresses).  
   • Unit: LIT (literal string).  
   • Default: “RLN” (frame + text + switch off the numeric value – so you’ll get only framed text such as “MAX=”).

5. How these parameters fit into the larger picture  
   • Showing logic (>0, =0, <0): by default any parameter > 0 forces display, = 0 suppresses it entirely, < 0 shows only when the sign of the quantity has changed.  
   • Zero text-size trick: if you set the global text size to zero (SIZE = 0), any annotation controlled by MAXR/MAXF/MPRP will be omitted entirely. This is handy for hiding inner-border dimensional lines or scale labels.  
   • Precision and format: number of decimal places is governed by ND (NDIM or NMAX settings) and by the SOFiSTiK unit definitions; very large values (> 1 × 10^7 by default) switch to E-format.  
   • Overlap avoidance (REVI/TREV): to prevent labels from overprinting each other, the system imposes a 0.7 mm grid. Each text element “claims” certain grid cells; if a new label would overlap more than the permitted percentage, it is either deleted or de-prioritized, according to your REVI/TREV settings.

In combination, MAXR, MAXF and MPRP give you fine-grained control over how maxima are highlighted in your 3D plot projections, both in terms of colour fills and extra text or framing. Use them alongside AMAX/MINV switches, COLO colour tables and the SCHH “legend” record to produce clear, customizable graphic output.

This is especially useful for dimensional lines of the inner border and for the FILL scale of the border at the left– hand side. The dimensional lines are defined with the unit 1001 of the SOFiSTiK-Units. The indicated scale as well as the dimensional lines refer to the three–dimensional representation of a line in the optical plane perpendicular to the line of vision.
 The decimal places of all values in the graph, the legend and the list output are uniformly based on what is specified in ND. With the input ND NDIM, the number of decimal places depends on the setting of the SOFiSTiK units. With the input ND NMAX the number of decimal places depends on the size of the value (compare also INTE SET 9). In the output, the values are rounded to the specified number of decimal places. Values that are smaller than can be represented with the number of decimal places are displayed as ’0.0’, if necessary with a sign. Large values, i.e. larger than the value INTE SET 9 PAR1 (default=1.E+7), are displayed in E format.
 The mutual overwriting of designation can be prevented with an input for REVI or TREV. For this the paper is divided into a grid (0.7 mm distance). Each lettering occupies a number of grid elements, where it is tested then, whether they were occupied already once from a previous lettering. The input parameter specifies, how much percent a lettering can retype another, that is how many grid elements. If this condition is not fulfilled, the designation is selected or deleted according to the input for TREV. This check needs more time, if it is performed more exactly. REVI does not affect the additional element designations (CURV, TEXT, NIVE, POST, AXIS).

Below is a structured, detailed description of the input-table and the meaning of each field.  This is intended to help a RAG/vector‐store ingest process understand what each parameter does, its units, legal values and defaults.

1. General Table Structure  
   • Four columns:  
     – Item: the short keyword used in the input deck.  
     – Description: full explanation of what the keyword controls and any sub-options.  
     – Unit: the data type or physical unit expected.  “LIT” means a literal keyword, “–/cm” means dimensionless or a length in cm, etc.  
     – Default: the value assumed if the keyword is omitted or set to the special literal DEFA.

2. MARK (Item)  
   • Purpose: controls whether and how a small marker (“cross”) is drawn at the text insertion point (sometimes called the effect point).  
   • Legal literals (Unit = LIT):  
     – NO   → no marker at all  
     – YES  → marker only when drawing QUAD or BRIC finite‐element results and in text mode (e.g. QUAD REPR DTXT)  
     – FULL → always draw marker whenever text is shown  
     – EXTR → always draw marker (even in extra modes)  
   • Default: YES

3. MHEI  
   • Purpose: height of the “cross” used for the MARK insertion-point marker.  If an underscore line accompanies the cross, its length is also derived from this.  
   • Value semantics (Unit = –/cm):  
     – > 0 : explicit height in cm  
     – < 0 : interpreted as a factor of the text height (see SCHH H6 for base text height)  
   • Default: –1.0  (i.e. one times the text height)

4. MFAC  
   • Purpose: factor controlling the length of the underscore relative to the MHEI cross-height.  
   • Unit: dimensionless  
   • Default: 2.0  (underscore is twice the cross-height)

5. PREF  
   • Purpose: prefix designations (e.g. load case number or design‐case index) before textual results.  
   • Legal literals (Unit = LIT):  
     – NO   → no prefix text  
     – YES  → prefix only for area‐load results  
     – FULL → prefix for all load‐type results  
     – EXTR → prefix for every result everywhere  
   • Default: NO

6. PROP  
   • Purpose: font styling for result text.  Either the default font or combinations of style flags.  
   • Legal literals (Unit = LIT):  
     – DEFA → normal font  
     – Any combination of:  
         • B  → bold  
         • I  → italic  
         • U  → underscore  
   • Default: DEFA

7. MAX1, MAX2, MAX3  
   • Purpose: maximum value thresholds for filtering text output in the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd result directions respectively.  
   • Interpretation:  
     – If set to DEFA, no maximum is applied (all results pass).  
     – If set to a numeric literal, only results less than (or, depending on other MIN/MAX logic, greater than) this threshold are drawn.  
     – See the general MIN/MAX rules (from the additional text) for combinations with BMIN, BMAX, etc.  
   • Unit: LIT  (literal numeric or DEFA)  
   • Defaults: all DEFA

8. Notes on MIN/MAX Logic (Context from Additional Text)  
   • DEFA means “use default” or “no limit.”  
   • Combinations of MIN-value and MAX-value follow these patterns:  
     – MIN DEFA & MAX DEFA → no filtering, all values valid  
     – MIN value & MAX DEFA → filter out anything below the minimum  
     – MIN DEFA & MAX value → filter out anything above the maximum  
     – MIN value1 & MAX value2 with value1 < value2 → only values in the open interval (value1, value2) pass  
     – MIN value1 & MAX value2 with value1 > value2 → values > value1 OR < value2 pass (wrap-around)

9. How the Table Affects Display  
   • The cross-marker size and underscore (MHEI, MFAC) define a small graphic placed behind or around text.  The background‐area size is also controlled by BACX/BACY/BMIN/BMAX elsewhere.  
   • Offsets (OFFS, FMVX, FMVY, MMIN, MMAX) and displacement types (DTYP, DVAR, DX, DY, DZ) let you fine-tune where the text and marker land relative to nodes, edges or element midpoints.  
   • FONT styling (PROP) and prefixes (PREF) control how the text is laid out semantically—whether you see load‐case numbers in front or special font flags.

By mapping each “Item” to its semantic role, legal inputs, units and default, this description provides a clear blueprint for parsing, validating, and storing these parameters in a vector‐based, retrieval‐augmented data store.

 DEFA no maximum value
 The unit of the minimum and maximum values refers to the results to just be drawn currently. Following combinations are possible:
 MIN DEFA and MAX DEFA :
 no selection, all values are valid
 MIN minvalue and MAX DEFA:
 Minimum values, values greater than minvalue are valid MIN DEFA and MAX maxvalue :
 Maximum values, values less than maxvalue are valid

 Value range, values greater than minvalue and less than
 maxvalue are valid
 MIN minvalue and MAX maxvalue and minvalue greater than maxvalue: Value ranges, values greater than minvalue or values less than maxvalue are valid
 If the literal DEFA is input for BACX, BACY, BMIN, BMAX, FMVX, FMVY, MMIN or MMAX, the corresponding default specified here is set.
 The result description is placed at a corresponding background area. This area can be bor- dered or the background can be deleted. The size of this area is controlled with BACX, BACY, BMIN or BMAX. In this case X is the writing direction and Y is the direction of the height.
 The result description is placed with the program control. However, an other offset can be also defined with OFFS, e.g. centrically at the corresponding place or next to that. It results the following orders:
 +2 +3 +4
 -1 0 +1
 -4 -3 -2
 The texts are drawn centrically at the insertion point with OFFS 0, with OFFS -4 to the left–hand side under that, with reference to the writing direction.
 The distance of the descriptions from the insertion point is defined with FMVX, FMVY, MMIN and MMAX. X and Y are here again the local writing directions.
 Usually the insertion point is displaced relatively to its original position a little bit, so that the descriptions in different direction (e.g. principal and transverse reinforcement of a plate) in the same node do not overwrite themselves. In this case the direction and the maximum value of the displacement (e.g. for QUAD elements the half element thickness) were determined already with GRAPHIC. However, the user can still change this with DTYP, DVAR, DX, DY and DZ.

 CM DVAR defines the distance in cm. The inputs for DX, DY and DZ are analysed.
 DX, DY and DZ are not analysed for the following literals. A defaulted direction is used:
 PROC DVAR defines the distance in % of the maximal allowable displacement.
 FACT DVAR defines the distance as factor of the text height.
 MINF as FACT, considering the maximum displacements
 MAXC DVAR defines the distance in cm.
 MINC as MAXC, considering the maximum displacements
 DX, DY and DZ are only analysed in the case of DTYP CM. Otherwise the direction defaulted by the program is used. The following literals are planned for DX:
 local x direction in the element
 X
 Y local y direction in the element
 Z local z direction in the element
 XX global X direction in the system
 YY global Y direction in the system
 ZZ global Z direction in the system
 EG global dead load direction
 URIC direction defined by the program, different according to the result type
 BX horizontal
 BY vertical
 PP perpendicular to the line direction to the right–hand side for line–like ele- ments
 PQ perpendicular to PP
 EP perpendicular to the line direction upwards for line–like elements
 EQ perpendicular to EP
 NM for line–like elements PP, else BX
 The direction is turned around with a ”–” sign before the literal. The direction can be input also as a global vector with DX, DY and DZ instead of a literal for DX.
